newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska row crop seedings nearly complete.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska row crop seedings nearly complete.

text.p: Nebraska corn, sorghum and soybean seedings neared completion, aided by weather conducive to fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn was rated one percent poor, 24 percent fair, 61 percent good and 14 percent excellent.
Soybeans were 94 percent emerged, ahead of 69 percent a year ago and above the 74 percent average pace. Soybeans were two percent poor, 26 percent fair, 62 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Sorghum seeding was 99 percent complete. The sorghum crop was three percent poor, 45 percent fair, 45 percent good and seven percent excellent.
The state's winter wheat crop rated one percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 41 fair, 40 percent good and six percent excellent.
Six percent of the crop was turning color, compared with 12 percent a year ago and 26 percent average.
Pasture conditions were eight percent poor, 24 percent fiar, 59 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was two percent very short, 22 percent short, 73 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
